problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Solving Systems of Equations Using Back Substitution

examples.knowledge_point: Solving a System of Equations Using Back Substitution Given an Augmented Matrix
examples.problem:
Solve the system of equations that is represented by the augmented matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071689/assets/1ecadec01586fecee4a8b6d8ad5015168387124430849ed2e7d884908e28e927.png)
examples.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say, $x_1,$ $x_2,$ and $x_3.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071689/assets/c7c7d0904aa85c2cd9915e95a8ca3cee9857deb216148f59372204c6672d8811.png)

The third equation states that $x_3=5.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
x_2+(5)=-2
	\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
	x_2=-2-5=-7.
$$

Now, we substitute both $x_3 = 5$ and $x_2 = -7$ into the first equation to get

$$
x_1+(-7)-(5) = 1
	\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
	x_1 = 1 + 7 + 5 = 13.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x_1 = 13,$ $x_2=-7,$ and $x_3 = 5.$ Or, in vector form, the solution is $\langle 13,-7,5 \rangle.$

feedback.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=9 \\  & {x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=2 \\  & {x}_{3}=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The third equation states that  ${x}_{3}=\frac{1}{3}.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}-3(\frac{1}{3})=2\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=2+1=3.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{3}=\frac{1}{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=3$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}-(3)+3(\frac{1}{3})=9\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=9+3-1=11.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=11$, ${x}_{2}=3$, and ${x}_{3}=\frac{1}{3}.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨11,3,\frac{1}{3}⟩.$
